info.name: Step-up elevation matrix (Slice C, ADR 0030 §5-9)
info.description: A supervisor's production contents open behind a FRESH second factor, for a bounded window. E1 the challenge, E2 the round trip, E4 the fingerprinting negatives, E5 members unaffected, E6 the human-only supervised path (through MCP), E7 the freshness drill, E3 the loop-prevention negative (inside the drill's shrunk window). Driven by run-step-up-matrix.sh, which mints the aal1/aal2 tokens with mint-code-flow-token.py — ROPC cannot carry auth_time. Fixture-id prefix f00d...

exec: "// The step-up assertions, shared. Postman has no module system, so they live in a collection",
"// variable and are eval'd by each script that needs them (the agent-tool matrix's idiom).",
"// EVERY pm.test callback here THROWS \u2014 a callback that merely RETURNS a boolean is ignored by",
"// newman and the cell passes unconditionally (E2E-TESTING, the assertion-style convention).",
"    pm.test(label + ': a well-formed RFC 9470 challenge', function () {",
"        // The window is the POLICY DATA's, never a local copy \u2014 the drill moves the data and",
"        // this parameter moves with it, which is what makes invariant 7 observable.",
"    pm.test(label + ': NO challenge is offered', function () {",
"    pm.test(label + ': the ordinary error code', function () {",
"    pm.test(label + ': 200 on the exact seeded id', function () {",
"    pm.test(label + ': 200 with exactly ' + ids.length + ' row(s), by id', function () {",
"// --- the MCP client, same framing as the agent-tool matrix -------------------",
"        if (node && (node.result !== undefined || node.error !== undefined)) { return node; }",
"    try { parsed = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { parsed = null; }",
"    return { isError: result.isError === true, layer: meta.layer || null,",
"             code: meta.code || null, text: text, json: parsed };",
"// A target-gate deny with the ORDINARY code is the whole agent assertion: had the policy",
"// leaked a challenge, the catalog service would have answered 401, the MCP translator would",
"// have labelled it 'catalog-unauthorized' with NO target-gate layer, and both expectations",
"// below would fail. The agent cells therefore assert the absence of a challenge structurally.",

item.name: Matrix
item.description: E1 the challenge · E2 the round trip · E4 the fingerprinting negatives · E5 members unaffected.

item.name: E1pre — the deny below is the TIER, not a missing role: anna reads the production CATALOG -> 200

exec: // The root read is metadata-only and carries no tier, so it opens for a supervisor at
// aal1 — and catalog.rego deliberately emits no deny_reason at all (a factor there would
// open nothing). Without this cell every 401 below could be 'anna has no role'.
pm.test('E1pre anna reaches the production catalog itself (200)', function () {
pm.test('E1pre and it is NOT a challenge', function () {

item.name: E1a — THE CHALLENGE: anna at aal1 lists the production catalog's categories -> 401

exec: // Slice B answered this with a plain 403. C's sole-blocker rule fires — anna IS granted,
// her token is not elevated, and no other deny applies — so the decision carries a
// structured deny_reason and the library's advice mints the RFC 9470 challenge.
stepUpChallenged('E1a the category LIST', pm.response, pm.environment.get('shipped_max_age'));

item.name: E1b — anna at aal1 GETs a category under the production catalog -> 401

exec: stepUpChallenged('E1b the category READ', pm.response, pm.environment.get('shipped_max_age'));

item.name: E1c — anna at aal1 GETs a product under the production catalog -> 401

exec: stepUpChallenged('E1c the product READ', pm.response, pm.environment.get('shipped_max_age'));

item.name: E1d — CONTROL: the same aal1 token on the UNTAGGED catalog's category -> 200

exec: // Non-production content is C-invariant: an ordinary aal1 supervisor keeps everything
// slice B gave her. Elevation only ever NARROWS what deny covers.
opened('E1d the untagged catalog stays open at aal1', pm.response,

item.name: E2a — THE ROUND TRIP: the same read with an aal2 token -> 200

exec: // One TOTP later, on the very same resource. Nothing was granted, nothing was tagged,
// no pod restarted — only the token's acr + auth_time moved.
opened('E2a the elevated category READ', pm.response,

exec: pageOfExactly('E2b the elevated category LIST', pm.response,

item.name: E2c — and the product below it -> 200

exec: opened('E2c the elevated product READ', pm.response,

exec: // sup-victor's unit does not reach this catalog, so his role never synthesizes and he is

item.name: E4b — THE WRITE CEILING: ELEVATED anna PUTs the production category -> plain 403

exec: // She is elevated and still denied: a supervisor's reach is read-only, which is not an
// elevation problem. `granted` is false for a write verb, so no reason is emitted and
// no challenge is offered — a TOTP prompt here would be an unfulfillable promise.

item.name: E5a — MEMBERS UNAFFECTED: the catalog's OWNER reads the production categories at plain aal1 -> 200

exec: // The owner's token is an ordinary ROPC one: acr aal1, no auth_time at all. Every C deny

// of it — and their _actions map stays honest and present.
pageOfExactly('E5a the owner\'s production category list', pm.response,

item.name: E6 agents
item.description: The supervised path is human-only: the target-gate cells over REST with the agent-client bearer, each paired with a same-subject human control.

item.name: E6a — the AGENT reads the PRODUCTION category -> plain 403, no challenge

exec: // The token is anna's own subject minted by an agent client, so it carries act_chain.
// The deny is the provenance-scoped agent clause, NOT the step-up clause — so the
// sole-blocker rule withholds the reason and no challenge is offered. A TOTP prompt to
// something that cannot answer one is the §7 loop, and this is where it is prevented.
plainDeny('E6a the agent on production', pm.response);

item.name: E6b — the AGENT reads the PRODUCTION product -> plain 403

exec: plainDeny('E6b the agent on the production product', pm.response);

item.name: E6c — ANY TIER: the AGENT reads the UNTAGGED catalog's category -> still plain 403

exec: // The supervised path is human-only in WHOLE, not only where the tier is production:
// supervision is a relation between people and a second factor proves a person is
// present. E1d read this very row at 200 with anna's human token.
plainDeny('E6c the agent on non-production content', pm.response);

item.name: E6d — the AGENT's catalog LIST -> membership-only, i.e. the empty page

exec: // `filter` never consults `denied` (invariant 5), so no rego clause can reach the
// supervised LIST leg — CatalogListAuthorizer skips it app-side when the subject
// carries the act_chain KEY. anna is a member of no team, so membership-only IS the
// empty page. 200 and empty, never 403: the leg is skipped, not denied.
pm.test('E6d the agent list answers 200', function () {
pm.test('E6d ...and carries no rows at all', function () {

item.name: E6i — THE ROOT TYPE: the AGENT reads the production CATALOG itself -> plain 403 (catalog.rego's supervised-agent deny; E1pre is the human 200 control)

exec: // The token is anna's own subject minted by an agent client, so it carries act_chain.
// The deny is the provenance-scoped agent clause, NOT the step-up clause — so the
// sole-blocker rule withholds the reason and no challenge is offered. A TOTP prompt to
// something that cannot answer one is the §7 loop, and this is where it is prevented.
plainDeny('E6i the agent on production', pm.response);

item.name: E6e — CONTROL: the SAME subject WITHOUT the claim reads that category -> 200

exec: // Without this cell E6c would be unfalsifiable: an empty reach and a closed door look
// identical from outside. Same person, same row, same tier — only the delegation claim
// differs, and that is what decides it.
opened('E6e the human reaches the same row', pm.response,

exec: // So E6d's empty page is the leg guard's doing and not an empty fixture set.
pm.test('E6f the human page carries both step-up catalogs', function () {

item.description: Defence in depth, and the measured reason the cells above are REST: the tool-gate's ceiling is membership-derived, so a pure supervisor is refused there before the target-gate is ever consulted.

exec: pm.test('the agent, through MCP handshake: the notification is 202 with an empty body', function () {

item.name: E6g — through MCP the AGENT never even reaches the target-gate: tool-gate deny

exec: // The tool-gate intersects the PRINCIPAL's ceiling with the agent capability, and
// that ceiling is membership-derived (permissions.effective_actions over the
// resolved role definition). A pure supervisor's reach comes from a reporting
// relation instead, so her ceiling is empty and the intersection is empty. The
// supervised path is therefore closed to agents at BOTH layers, tool-gate first.
mcpDenied('E6g the agent is refused at the tool-gate', pm.response,

item.name: E6h — ...and so is anna HERSELF: the MCP ceiling is membership-derived

exec: // The same call E6e answered 200 over REST. This is the measured reason the
// target-gate cells above are REST rather than MCP: through the tool surface a
// pure supervisor is refused before her provenance is ever consulted, so an MCP
// 403 would prove the tool-gate and say nothing about C's agent deny.
mcpDenied('E6h the pure supervisor has no tool-gate ceiling at all', pm.response,

item.name: E7a drill positive control
E7a — POSITIVE CONTROL: a FRESH elevation still opens production under the 5s override -> 200

exec: // The override is a LEAF PUT (/v1/data/step_up/max_age). A whole-document PUT would have
// replaced the object and taken `loa` and `skew` with it — and then EVERY token would be
// unelevatable and the 401 below would arrive instantly and prove nothing. This cell is
// what makes the expiry cell honest.
opened('E7a a fresh elevation under the shrunk window', pm.response,

item.name: E7b drill expiry
E7b — ...and after the window closes, the SAME token answers 401 again

exec: // The very same bearer that answered 200 a moment ago. Nothing about the token changed —
// no expiry, no revocation, no refresh — only wall-clock time passed. The freshness
// control is the only thing that can have moved.
stepUpChallenged('E7b the elevation has expired on the wire', pm.response, pm.environment.get('drill_max_age'));

item.name: E3 loop prevention
E3 — LOOP PREVENTION: re-auth WITHOUT max_age reuses the SSO session -> still 401

exec: // A brand-new access token, minted seconds ago, carrying acr aal2 — and the SAME stale
// auth_time, because the SSO session answered and no authentication happened. ADR 0030
// §7's 'the client MUST forward max_age', measured: a client that drops it loops forever.
// The runner asserted auth_time(stale) == auth_time(drill) shell-side before this ran.
stepUpChallenged('E3 the SSO-reused token is still not elevated', pm.response, pm.environment.get('drill_max_age'));
pm.test('E3 the stale token really is a NEWER token (iat advanced)', function () {
